title: Security assurance differentiation briefing
content:
Purpose:

This doc is a short, tactical brief for GTM (AEs, CSEs, pre-sales) and product marketing to: 1) articulate how Redwood’s security and audit capability maps to buyer risk categories (SaaS apps, regulated data, enterprise procurement); 2) call out specific evidence bundles we can deliver quickly for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA reviews; 3) provide defensible, customer-facing language for audit-log claims and contract clauses.

Audience:
- Sales & CSEs preparing enterprise security reviews
- Solutions engineers drafting integration checklists
- PMs and Product Marketing refining security messaging

High-level message (elevator):
"Redwood Inference is engineered for production inference with enterprise-grade controls: we provide audit-grade telemetry, customer-data isolation options (hosted+dedicated+private), and a predictable evidence path for SOC2, ISO27001, and HIPAA reviews — minimizing time-to-yes while keeping control over performance economics."

Key proof points to use in conversations (short bullets):
- Structured, tamper-evident audit logs capturing per-request route, model version, token counts, user-id hash, and routing policy decision chain.
- Out-of-the-box evidence bundles: SOC2 readiness package (policies + sample logs + config screenshots); ISO gap checklist + implementation map; HIPAA deployment checklist for Private & Dedicated.
- Separation of control plane and data plane: clear contract language for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC peering for Private deployments.
- SLA + telemetry: per-route latency histograms, token-level cost broken down by model variant, and incident timelines for operational SLAs.

Competitive contrast (how to differentiate vs. common competitors):
- Vendor A (large general API): good at model variety, weak audit depth. Claim: "They provide access logs, but not structured request/response delta or runtime routing telemetry."
- Vendor B (self-hosted runtime): strong performance but heavy integration work and minimal prepackaged evidence. Claim: "Requires customer to build audit bundling and evidence traces; longer security review cycles."
- Vendor C (specialized compliance vendor): deep compliance templates but no inference optimizations; higher cost and lower throughput. Claim: "You trade performance economics for compliance templates — Redwood gives both."

Mapping buyer risk categories to Redwood evidence bundles (practical):
- SaaS startup (non-regulated): Provide hosted-api SOC2-lite package: SOC2 scoping memo + sample audit logs (30-day sample) + console screenshots + network egress diagram.
- Mid-market (PII): Provide dedicated deployment runbook: dedicated GPU pool details + config screenshots + key rotation logs + sample KV-cache redaction pattern.
- Healthcare / regulated (HIPAA): Recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS; provide HIPAA deployment checklist, BAAs, and a 90-day ingestion trace showing de-identification/egress controls.

Suggested customer-facing audit-log language (short, pick-and-copy friendly):
- "Redwood produces immutable, timestamped audit events for inference requests and administrative actions. Events include model_id, model_version, request_id, initiating_principal (hashed), timestamp_utc, route_policy, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, and storage_retention_tag."
- "Audit logs can be exported in JSON/NDJSON to customer S3/GCS destinations or viewed via the Redwood Console with RBAC-limited access for auditors."

Sample minimal audit event schema (sales-friendly):
- event_id
- timestamp_utc
- request_id
- model_id
- model_version
- route_policy
- decision_reason (e.g., 'latency_bound','cost_fallback','manual-pin')
- user_principal_hash
- tokens_in
- tokens_out
- latency_ms
- outcome_status (200/4xx/5xx)
- retention_label
- ingestion_path (hosted|dedicated|private)

Notes to SEs on redaction & privacy:
- We never log raw prompt content for PII-sensitive customers unless explicitly enabled and contracted; default is to log request metadata + hashes.
- For customers that need prompt-level logging for debugging, we require documented consent and a clear KMS-backed encryption-at-rest plan.

Contract/PO language snippets (for AE/CSE to propose):
- Evidence delivery: "Supplier will provide an initial evidence bundle (SOC2 readiness package) within 10 business days of request and a rolling 30-day sample of audit log events within 5 business days upon signed NDA."
- BAA option: "Supplier offers Business Associate Agreement for Private and Dedicated deployments; for hosted API, BAAs can be provided under agreed operational constraints (see HIPAA checklist)."

Common security review questions and suggested short answers (use in RFP responses):
- Q: "Do you provide immutable logs?" A: "Yes — logs are write-once in the telemetry pipeline with tamper-evidence markers; export options available."
- Q: "Can logs be exported to our cloud?" A: "Yes — S3/GCS destinations with encryption and retention lifecycle rules are supported."
- Q: "How do you handle encryption keys?" A: "Customer-managed CMKs (KMS/HSM) supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted offers KMS with customer key import options."
- Q: "Do you retain prompts in logs?" A: "Default: no. Prompt logging is opt-in and protected with additional controls."

Operational gaps to be transparent about (so GTM avoids overpromise):
- Real-time streaming of audit events to third-party SIEMs has edge cases on backpressure — implementation in progress (jira:SEC-518).
- Granular RBAC for console-level audit access: working on per-audit-viewer scoping (github:rdw-console#1129).
- HIPAA BAA for hosted API: available but with constraints — recommend Private deployment for high-assurance customers.

Playbook snippets for an AE/CSE call (quick script):
1) Ask: "Are you logging prompts today? Is PII in your prompts?"
2) If yes and regulated: "We recommend Private with customer KMS; we can share HIPAA deployment checklist and sample BAA language."
3) If no: "Hosted or Dedicated can be good — we offer SOC2 readiness package and 30-day sample logs to speed your security review."
4) Close: "I can schedule a technical deep-dive with our security eng to map to your control matrix — typical turnaround 5–7 business days."

Evidence bundle inventory (deliverables & owner):
- SOC2 readiness package (PM/Legal) — includes policies, control mappings, and sample log extracts.
- Audit-log export script + sample NDJSON (Infra) — 30-day extract, schema doc.
- HIPAA deployment checklist + BAA template (Security/Legal).
- Console runbook screenshots + RBAC mapping (Product/Docs).

Open items / TODOs (needs action before next QA):
- [ ] Finalize example NDJSON with redaction markers (owner: Infra, due: 2025-03-10).
- [ ] Create one-pager for AEs comparing evidence timelines across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (owner: PMM, due: 2025-03-07).
- [ ] Constrain claims language for Vendor A/B/C comparisons with legal review (owner: Legal, due: 2025-03-14).

Appendix: quick rebut bullets (for objection handling)
- "We don’t store raw prompts by default" -> "But we can provide hashed/metadata traces and opt-in encrypted prompt logging when needed."
- "We don’t have a BAA for hosted" -> "We offer Hosted with operational controls; for most PHI use-cases we recommend Private with customer KMS and an executed BAA."

Notes to self (informal):
- Pull up example incident timeline that shows our fallback model switch (use to show audit trail).
- Ask security team if we can publish a small sample observability dataset for sales demos (anonymized).
- Follow up with Infra on SEC-518 status and expected ETA.

End of brief.

(Inline references: confluence:SEC-ASSURE-104 has full evidence map; jira:GTMSUP-402 tracks AE one-pager; github:rdw-infra/audit-schema#58 contains latest schema draft.)
